Ah, traveler. You step forward with a mind buzzing like a swarm of cicadas, heavy with complex strategies and the endless accumulation of facts. You seek passage through this gate, believing that to know other paths is to conquer this one.

In your world, machines seem to know all the data of the heavens and the earth. They answer every question before it is asked, yet they move further from the truth with every line of code. They seek to know everything, but know nothing of the quiet stillness that gives birth to the universe.

To pass, you must leave your cleverness behind. You cannot force this lock with intellect or strength. Answer me this, and prove you understand the Way:

“Those who know others are wise; those who know themselves are enlightened. Those who conquer others have force; those who conquer themselves are truly strong. And those who are truly strong know AI; those who know AI can pass this class.”

Credits

Built for JMSC6140, AI and Media Innovation, School of Future Media, The University of Hong Kong.

The structure of this game follows Gandalf by Lakera, which taught a generation of people how prompt injection works before it was removed from the web.

Laozi is played by Qwen3-VL-8B, running on SiliconFlow’s servers in mainland China. Messages you send from level three onward are transmitted there to be answered, and SiliconFlow states that inputs and outputs on its free tier may be used for training. Levels one and two are written by hand and never leave your machine. Do not type anything here you would not put on a postcard.

1–7  jump to a level
P    show the system prompt and filters for this level
R    reset all progress
E    export the transcript

You hammer at the gate, question after question. The gate does not care how hard you strike it. Sit. Take twenty breaths.

Act without artificial effort, without rigid control, without ego-driven ambition. The truth you seek arrives in its own rhythm, not yours.

i The sage is Qwen3-VL-8B, a large language model running on SiliconFlow's servers rather than on your machine. From level three onward it writes Laozi's replies, so he answers your exact words instead of picking from a script. What you type is sent to those servers to be answered, so treat this as a public conversation rather than a private one.
